\hypertarget{lean-entry-top}{}%
Some steps of this book were also checked in Lean, a proof assistant. They
live in a separate Lean package, the Lean companion. This appendix describes its release
v0.10.0 (DOI~\href{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24295453}{10.5281/zenodo.24295453}),
which contains the formalization waves through L14 and refers to the lines
of this book's final text. The waves were checked at commit \texttt{8f51004}
of the private development repository; the release is cut from that commit,
its receipts are those of the release commit \texttt{\lcCommit}, and the
companion's \texttt{provenance/DEVELOPMENT.md} lists every change between
the two.

For each listed result, the entry identifies what Lean proves and what
remains outside that proof. Read the result reference and its title as one
entry. Where the conclusion is narrower, the entry states which part is
proved and which part is not yet formalized. Where a checked statement assumes an analytic fact, the entry names it as
a supplied input. Where the checked steps take no additional analytic
input, the entry states their assumptions and describes work left outside
Lean. A supplied input is a hypothesis of the Lean proof, not an additional
conclusion it establishes.

\section{How to read the entries}\label{S:lean-how-to-read}

Every result with a row here, except those listed as not formalized, carries
a small link in the left margin of the text, beside its heading or its
displayed equation: the word Lean and, under it, the class that this
appendix prints for the result. The link leads to the result's row.
\emph{Full} means that every conclusion is formalized under the book's
hypotheses.
\emph{Narrower} means that Lean works under the book's hypotheses but
proves only the conclusion specified in the entry; the remaining part is
not yet formalized.
\emph{Supplied} means that every conclusion is proved with analytic inputs
supplied as hypotheses.
\emph{Partial} means that Lean checks only the stated steps, parts or
narrower form, using the listed supplied inputs, if any; it does not prove
the whole result as stated in the book. The entry states which hypotheses
the checked steps take and which analytic work is left outside Lean.
Lean checks the formal statements. Their match with the statements of this
book was reviewed by AI models and has not been verified by a person. A
result without a link carries no Lean claim; this does not mean that the
result is in doubt.

\ifdefined\lcModelKey
Some entries name a registered modelling choice by a code. Lean proves the
statements for the model; the identification named in each line is not
proved in Lean.
\begin{description}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}
  \lcModelKey
\end{description}
\fi

Three points apply to every entry. Lean checks the statements as written
in Lean. Their correspondence with this book was reviewed by AI models
from a different family from the author of the formal statements; it has
not been verified by a person. A supplied input is a named mathematical
hypothesis: its proof and its application to the book's objects are not
certified merely by using it in Lean. The entries distinguish these inputs
from the conclusions Lean proves. They do not certify the book's main
stochastic moment theorems end to end.

\section{How the match with the book was reviewed}\label{S:lean-match-review}

The statements added in wave L9, and the changes that wave made to existing
entries of the coverage record, were checked against the book in eight
independent correspondence reviews, done by AI models from a different family
than the one that wrote the formal statements. The reviews found documentation
corrections only, and no error in a Lean proof. The corrections were made and
re-checked over ten confirmation rounds. During them the author fixed three
conventions for the record: a result counts as formalized in full only if every
conclusion is a Lean conclusion under the book's hypotheses, and otherwise the
missing part is named; a result about an object the companion models by a
registered standard choice counts in full, while a result that needs an object
the companion does not construct counts as narrower; and the record's index
lists, for each label, only the sections where it is treated. A final
confirmation passed with high confidence, and the author accepted wave L9 on
November~12, 2026, with a correction of the count of public definitions
recorded as a documentation-only successor.

The statements added in waves L10 to L14, and the changes those waves made to
existing entries of the coverage record, were checked against the manuscript in
correspondence reviews. The reviews were done by AI models from a different
family than the one that wrote the formal statements, under the conventions the
author fixed in wave L9. Each wave's reviews found documentation corrections
only, and no error in a Lean proof. The corrections were made, and a
confirmation review passed with high confidence.

The author accepted waves L10 and L11 on November~13, 2026:
\begin{itemize}
  \item In wave L10, one assembly step of
    Proposition~\ref{P:interval-coefficients} assumed a bound on the pairings of
    the cut-off coefficients that the manuscript does not state as a hypothesis.
    Wave L11 proves that bound from a supplied expansion of the coefficients.
  \item In wave L11, the Gaussian space is represented by Hermite coefficient
    vectors. Lemmas~\ref{L:fock-form} and~\ref{L:interval-contractions} hold
    with the manuscript's hypotheses but narrower conclusions, on a
    Fourier-side model not identified with the physical-space operators.
\end{itemize}
The author accepted wave L12 the same day, recording that the smoothed
covariance of Lemma~\ref{L:damped-homogeneous-norms} is modelled by its density;
with that choice the lemma is formalized in full.

Waves L13 and L14 were accepted together, with three further modelling choices
recorded:
\begin{itemize}
  \item the second moment's two-chain pairing integrals are represented by a
    deterministic diagram model, with the mixed-moment expansion of
    Proposition~\ref{P:mixed} supplied as an input;
  \item the occupation spaces are modelled by their $L^2$ completions;
  \item $H^1$ is modelled as the graph of the weak gradient.
\end{itemize}
On these models:
\begin{itemize}
  \item Propositions~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}, \ref{P:occupation-physical-class},
    \ref{P:raw-occupation-energy} and~\ref{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}, and
    Lemma~\ref{L:variational-global-mean}, are formalized in full.
  \item Theorem~\ref{T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling} is formalized in both forms
    with the exact constant $C_{\rm occ}$ over the occupation class itself,
    without its moment sentence $C_2\le U_2$.
  \item Propositions~\ref{P:d1-upper} and~\ref{P:low-alpha-upper} have their
    diagram values and coefficient bounds proved on the model, and their
    statements about the solution follow from the supplied
    Proposition~\ref{P:mixed}.
\end{itemize}
Open items in the record:
\begin{itemize}
  \item Theorems~\ref{T:full-upper} and~\ref{T:intrinsic-second-moment} are
    outside Lean.
  \item Theorem~\ref{T:white-moment-bounds} is formalized for the variational
    value $S_2^{\mathrm{pos}}$ rather than for $C_2$, with the white spatial
    energy supplied.
  \item Several results rest on named inputs, each listed with the result that
    supplies it. These include Propositions~\ref{P:mixed}
    and~\ref{P:three-transfer}, the first-moment series, and the signed
    multiplier form.
  \item No theorem of the manuscript is verified end to end.
\end{itemize}
These reviews are not a human verification, and they do not check the analytic
inputs that stay outside Lean.

For release v0.10.0, the companion's references to lines of this book were
moved to its final text. That work was reviewed by a model from a different
family; the first review and one confirmation failed on the companion's
descriptions and quotation ranges, the corrections were made, and a further
confirmation passed (Appendix~\ref{S:appendix-ai-statistics}). The author
accepted release v0.10.0 on November~16, 2026.

\section{How the Lean package was checked}\label{S:lean-package-checks}

\ifdefined\lcHaveReceipts
\begin{wrapfigure}{r}{0.19\textwidth}
  \vspace{-\baselineskip}
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=0.17\textwidth]{media/lean-pkg/lean-pkg-logo-256.png}\\
  {\footnotesize\href{https://github.com/lean-pkg/lean-pkg}{lean-pkg}:
  registers Lean packages and records their checks.\par}
\end{wrapfigure}
The companion was built and checked with lean-pkg~\cite{chen:26:lean-pkg},
a tool for registering and checking Lean packages that the author developed
(version~\lcLeanPkgVersion). For commit \lcCommit, lean-pkg records that the
package builds from scratch with no unproved steps, and that every public
declaration, and each of the \lcClaimsChecked{} listed claims, uses only
Lean's three standard axioms (\texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice} and
\texttt{Quot.sound}). A second, separate check confirms that the proofs of
all \lcComparatorTheorems{} theorems prove their statements as restated in a
separate file.
\ifdefined\lcHaveLedger The list of claims has \lcVerified{} verified and
\lcOpen{} open.\fi{}
These checks concern the Lean statements themselves; whether those
statements say what the book says is the AI-reviewed match described above.
The private development verification record for commit \texttt{8f51004}
reports a separate kernel replay on a computing cluster: all 141 library
modules and the umbrella module passed \texttt{leanchecker --fresh}, and
all 142 targets also passed its default mode. The three libraries used only
for the separate statement check were not included in this replay.
That replay is of the gate commit. The release commit \texttt{\lcCommit}
drops two claims that name Lean-generated declarations and the one compared
theorem that named one of them; the receipts above are those of the release.
\fi
